$BNB has fallen more moderately than $ETH this time around, and that comparison is the most noteworthy thing today.

$BNB is currently at 585.2, down 1.3% over 24 hours, while $ETH is down 3.1% over the same period—more than twice as much. But looking back over 7 and 30 days, both have been trending downward in tandem: $BNB is down 13.9% over seven days and 20.1% over 30 days, while $ETH is down 14.2% and 26.7%, respectively. In other words, this isn't a divergence within the sector: both platform tokens and ETH-related assets are being dragged down by the broader market. $BNB has simply fallen more slowly over the past few hours, which doesn't mean it has escaped this correction.

Both coins are now stuck in pretty ugly positions. The daily RSI(14) is just 26 for $BNB and 24 for $ETH, both nearing oversold territory. $BNB ranks in just the 10th percentile of its 30-day range, while $ETH is even worse, at the 7th percentile. All the moving averages are above price and weighing on it: $BNB is 3.4% below MA7 and 13.8% below MA25. This is a classic bearish moving-average setup, and the moving averages aren't likely to turn into support in the short term.

There's one detail I think matters more than the percentage losses: $BNB's 24-hour trading volume is 81.25 million USDT, just 0.9 times its average daily volume over the past seven days. It's falling on lower volume, not being aggressively sold off. My own habit when watching the market is to check volume first when prices are falling. A decline on lower volume suggests selling pressure isn't accelerating; it looks more like a gradual slide driven by momentum after sentiment has cooled. A true panic bottom is often accompanied by a surge in volume, and we haven't seen that yet. This is a more useful way to assess the market than just looking at the percentage drop, and it's a habit worth developing.

In the community, people are discussing the transfer of more than 70,000 ETH from a wallet linked to a hacking incident. There are also rumors that a wallet associated with a well-known figure continued adding to its ETH position while at a loss. These claims can't be verified, but they do show that market sentiment has turned negative, with people looking for reasons to explain the drop.

My view is that the short-term outlook is probably choppy with a downward bias. The reasons are the moving-average setup and the position within the range described above. An RSI of 26 means an oversold bounce could happen at any time, but that doesn't change the fact that the broader trend won't stabilize unless price moves above MA7 at 605.7 on strong volume. If $BNB falls below this cycle's 30-day low of 566, then my read is wrong and the bears are stronger than I thought.

#BNB #ETH #PlatformTokens

content:
$BNB这轮跌得比$ETH克制一些，这个对比是今天最值得看的点。

$BNB现价585.2，24小时跌1.3%，而$ETH同期跌3.1%，跌幅差了一倍多。但往回看7天和30天，两者其实是同向下探的：$BNB七日跌13.9%、三十日跌20.1%，$ETH七日跌14.2%、三十日跌26.7%。也就是说这不是板块分化，是整个平台币和ETH系一起被大盘按下去，$BNB只是这几个小时跌得慢一点，不代表它逃过了这轮回调。

两个币现在都卡在很难看的位置。$BNB日线RSI14只有26，$ETH是24，都逼近超卖区；$BNB在30日区间里只排在10%的位置，$ETH更惨，排在7%。均线全部在价格上方压着，$BNB现价比MA7低3.4%，比MA25低13.8%，这种排列就是典型的空头排列，短期内均线不会反过来帮你。

有一个细节我觉得比涨跌幅更重要：$BNB这24小时成交额8125万USDT，只有过去7天日均的0.9倍，是缩量在跌，不是放量砸盘。我自己看盘习惯是，跌的时候先看量能，缩量阴跌说明抛压没有加速，更像是情绪钝化后的惯性下滑；真正的恐慌底往往伴随放量，现在还没看到。这个辨别方法比光看跌幅有用，建议养成这个习惯。

社区那边，有人在讨论和黑客事件关联的钱包转移了七万多枚ETH，也有传言说和某个知名人物相关的钱包在亏损状态下继续加仓ETH，这类消息真假没法核实，但能看出市场情绪已经偏负面，大家在找理由解释跌。

我自己的看法是，短期大概率先震荡偏弱，理由就是上面这套均线排列和区间位置，RSI压到26说明超卖反弹随时可能来一下，但不改变大方向需要放量站上MA7这条605.7才算企稳的事实。如果$BNB跌破这轮30日低点566，那就说明我这个判断错了，空头比我想的更有力。

Fed Governor Discusses Tokenized Settlement | ETH Needs Real Usage to Benefit | Stay Disciplined Below 1,800

My stance is cautious; I’m not chasing ETH just because of a speech by a central bank official. On November 17, Fed Governor Waller gave a public speech on the intersection of payments and tokenized markets: assets such as stocks and bonds can be tokenized, and transactions also require programmable payment tools. He cited stablecoins and tokenized deposits, and explicitly mentioned early DeFi lending and trading with assets such as Bitcoin and Ethereum. This speech addressed the industry’s direction and risks; it was neither an announcement that the Fed would adopt Ethereum nor approval of any ETH product. Treating a mention of “Ethereum” as an official endorsement would mislead trading decisions.

The section on “trust” stood out to me most. Waller raised questions of liability involving smart-contract fraud, lost keys, erroneous transfers, pricing errors, and failed on-chain assets. He also said governance, legal frameworks, and data standards are just as important as technology. The potential transmission mechanism for ETH is this: if institutions are willing to settle on public networks in the future, activity involving stablecoins, tokenized assets, and collateral could boost on-chain demand. But if most activity takes place on bank-built or consortium chains, or fees are ultimately absorbed by layer-2 networks, ETH’s value capture on mainnet cannot be extrapolated linearly from transaction volume. We need to watch actual settlement volumes, fees, and security records—not just the speech’s headline.

So far, the market reaction does not support the claim that “the policy tailwind has already materialized.” ETH/USDT was around $1,793.10 on Binance, down about 1.68% over 24 hours, with a low of 1,751.39 and a high of 1,836. Farside data showed net outflows of $29.1 million from U.S. spot ETH funds on November 17: $27.6 million from ETHA and $2.8 million from ETHB. Data for November 18 is still incomplete, so the page’s 0.0 cannot be used to claim that flows have already reversed. Current Binance Square trending topics focus on the Bank of England’s DLT settlement path, institutional access to stablecoins, and security incidents. Waller’s speech falls under the same broader discussion of payment infrastructure, but I haven’t seen a matching, accurately named trending-topic tag, so I’m only adding the ETH ticker tag.

For trading, first watch whether the low near 1,750 holds, then whether ETH can reclaim and hold 1,800; 1,835 is the recent upper boundary. If 1,750 breaks and a rebound attempt fails, it would suggest that investors are still reducing risk and that the tokenization narrative alone is not enough to support the price. I’d only consider shifting from cautious to bullish if verifiable data emerges on institutional mainnet settlements, ETF inflows recover, and price reclaims 1,835 on strong volume. If it’s merely a newly built permissioned chain or a one-off trial, the original view that Ethereum mainnet will benefit needs to be downgraded.

If I were trading this myself, I’d stay out for now, with a neutral bias and a 0% position. I’d only try a long with 2% of total capital after ETH spot holds above 1,800 for two consecutive 4-hour candles, successfully retests that level, and volume improves. The first target is 1,835; I’d take half off there and target 1,870 with the rest. After entry, I’d stop out if a 4-hour candle closes back below 1,775. If 1,750 breaks, ETF outflows widen, or settlement cases confirm no connection to Ethereum mainnet, I’d close the remaining position. No high leverage; if the conditions aren’t met, I’ll stay flat.

#ETH
The above is only my personal market observation and does not constitute investment advice.

content:
美联储理事谈代币化结算｜ETH受益要靠真实用量｜1800下方先守纪律

我的态度偏谨慎，暂不因一场央行官员讲话追买ETH。美联储理事Waller在11月17日公开演讲讨论支付与代币化市场的交汇：股票、债券等资产可被代币化，交易同时还需要可编程的支付工具；他列举稳定币和代币化存款，也明确提到DeFi早期以比特币、以太坊等资产开展借贷和交易。这是一份关于行业方向与风险的讲话，既不是美联储宣布采用以太坊，也不是批准某个ETH产品。将“提到Ethereum”直接写成官方背书，会误导交易判断。

讲话中我更重视“信任”一段。Waller提出智能合约欺诈、密钥丢失、错误转账、定价失误和失败链上资产的责任归属；他还说治理、法律框架、数据标准与技术一样重要。对ETH的传导机制是：若机构未来愿意在公开网络上进行结算，稳定币、代币化资产和抵押品活动可能增加链上需求；但若业务主要落在银行自建链、联盟链，或者费用最终由二层网络吸收，主网ETH的价值捕获就不能按交易规模线性外推。需要观察真实结算量、费用和安全记录，而不是只看演讲标题。

市场反应暂不支持“政策利好已兑现”的说法。查看币安ETH/USDT时约1793.10美元，24小时跌约1.68%，区间低点1751.39、高点1836。Farside统计的11月17日美国现货ETH基金合计净流出2910万美元，ETHA流出2760万、ETHB流出280万；18日数据仍未完整形成，不能用页面的0.0声称资金已经转向。币安广场当前热点集中在英央行DLT清算路径、机构稳定币接入及安全事件。Waller讲话与这些主题同属支付基础设施讨论，但我没有看到对应的准确上升话题标签，因此只加ETH币种标签。

交易上先看1750附近的低点能否守住，再看1800能否重新站稳；1835是近期上沿。若1750失守且反抽失败，说明资金仍在减风险，本轮代币化叙事不足以支撑价格。若后续出现可核实的机构主网结算数据、ETF流入修复，同时价格放量收复1835，才考虑把观点从谨慎转为偏多。若只是新建许可链或一次性试验，原本的主网受益判断就需要下调。

如果是我自己交易，目前不参与，方向中性、仓位0。仅在ETH现货连续两根4小时K线站稳1800、回踩不破且成交改善后，用总资金2%试多；目标先看1835，触及减半，余仓看1870。入场后若4小时收盘跌回1775就止损；若1750破位、ETF流出扩大或结算案例证实与以太坊主网无关，就平掉余仓。全程不用高杠杆，条件没触发便保持空仓。

#ETH
以上仅为个人市场观察，不构成投资建议。

$STRK: Same Hourly Drop, Divergent Volume Signals

The hourly candle for $STRK is down with volume above baseline, yet the two peer assets show the same directional move with opposite volume readings. This contrast raises a question: does a shared price direction carry the same implication when participation differs?

A tempting shortcut assumes that any down candle with elevated activity reflects a single broad force. The observations for $ETH and $MMT break that pattern. One peer matches $STRK with volume above baseline, the other shows a down candle without that volume lift. Because relative volume 2.40x baseline is a ratio against preceding candles .  not a measure of buying pressure, order flow, or capital rotation .  the similarity in direction does not imply a common cause.

A more careful interpretation treats the volume divergence as a conditional signal. If $STRK sustains its hourly decline while relative volume reverts toward baseline, the current participation spike may have been transient. Conversely, if volume stays elevated through subsequent closed candles, the down move could reflect deeper conviction. The RSI reading 30.9 adds context but does not confirm exhaustion or capitulation; indicators are readings, not price bounds.

A useful next observation would track whether $STRK volume remains above baseline on the next hourly close. A return to baseline while price continues lower would weaken the idea that the current volume spike signals sustained conviction. Until then, the divergent peer behavior serves as a reminder that same-venue hourly differences have limits and should not be extrapolated into a shared narrative.

Probabilistic market research, not a recommendation or guaranteed return.

The code did one nasty thing after another: when you copied a wallet address to make a transfer, it secretly swapped in the hackers’ address. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, TRON, and Dogecoin were all targeted. It also stole any bank card number, expiration date, and CVV you entered on a website, along with browser cookies, and took screenshots. iPhones and iPads running older operating systems were also vulnerable to an exploit kit.

The attack was discovered by British security researcher Scott Helme, who first spotted the injection in BBC’s code in the early hours of November 16. By that evening, TalkTalk was the only company that hadn’t fully cleaned it up. The hackers’ wallet has been tracked receiving about $7,000 in cryptocurrency. It’s not yet known how much was stolen through bank cards.

Optimizely admitted that the hackers had exploited a vulnerability in its registration process to impersonate users and inject the code. It said the vulnerability had been fixed and the code removed. Apple also said the exploited iOS vulnerability was patched last year, and that updating to the latest operating system will keep you safe.

If you copied a wallet address on any of these major websites on November 16, be sure to check that the address you paste is your own before making a transfer.

The biggest misconception beginners have: if you’re not holding a position, you’re not trading. So they stay fully invested, buying and selling every day,
until fees and market swings wear away their capital.

Stay flat when bulls and bears are battling it out, and after a string of losing trades—the money you save at these three moments,
is more than most people make from trading.

You may be tired of hunting metaphors, but the point is true: hunters spend most of their time waiting. Pulling the trigger
takes just a second. Keep your capital intact, and when an opportunity comes, you’ll have a bullet to fire. Hold on to your bullets.

translatedData.subTitle:
Most people spend 90% of their time predicting the market and 0% reviewing their own trades. They’ve got it backwards.

Write down three things for every trade: why you entered (your rationale), what went right or wrong (in your execution), and
what you’ll do differently next time (a specific action). Stick with it for a month, and you’ll be surprised to discover that your losses
The same types of mistakes keep showing up in your trade history—for example, always reversing your position right after a stop-loss,
or never holding on to winning trades.

The market changes, but your behavioral patterns won’t change on their own unless you keep an eye on them and work to change them. The market is the most
honest teacher, and your trade history is your report card. Don’t just look at your account balance—go through your trading records.

On the evening of November 17, on-chain sleuth Lookonchain reported that the hackers had a huge pool of 602402 ETH worth $1.09 billion, all stolen funds waiting to be laundered. The irony is that THORChain’s token, RUNE, is actually up 7%, at $0.55. The more the hackers launder, the more it earns in fees. When Bybit was hacked last year, THORChain processed $4.66 billion in swaps in just one week.

📰 Has the crypto oracle become a contrarian indicator? Hayes called for an ETH rally, then dumped $8.5M

Arthur Hayes said just a few days ago that ETH was going to rise. But a wallet linked to him then transferred 4,700 ETH (worth $8.5M) to Coinbase in a single transaction. This crypto veteran, once a soothsayer of the “four biggest trends before the AI bubble,” has suddenly become a bona fide ETH seller.

Why does this news matter?
Hayes’s previous comments about ETH fit the classic bullish narrative driven by the “celebrity effect.” As the founder of BitMEX, his remarks can typically give market sentiment a short-lived boost. But what matters more than his opinion itself is the flow of funds—from “talking up the market” to “moving real money out.” This behavior may be more informative than a simple prediction. It could signal Hayes’s concerns about ETH’s current price, or, more likely, an asset allocation adjustment, moving liquid funds to a safer platform such as Coinbase.

Market impact
In the short term, this transaction will draw attention from ETH bears, especially around the key $63,238 level. But ETH’s price is shaped by complex factors, and Hayes’s personal trading activity is more of a sentiment indicator than a decisive factor. This means ETH’s short-term volatility could increase, while the long-term trend still depends on the AI market and Ethereum’s fundamentals. There have been similar cases in the past: in 2019, after Musk tweeted that BTC was too expensive, BTC actually rose 15% that day. This shows that celebrity behavior and the market’s actual reaction can sometimes diverge.

Trading approach
This transaction suggests selling pressure on ETH above $63,238, but it is not enough to change the medium-term bullish trend. If ETH can hold this level, it would indicate that bearish pressure has been absorbed. However, be wary: if more linked transactions start flowing out in quick succession, this support level could fail. If the market ultimately validates Hayes’s view, ETH could indeed have upside potential before the AI bubble.

Made $25 million in 12 seconds. The judge said: not guilty—Ethereum never had a user agreement.

On November 16, U.S. Manhattan federal judge Jessica Clarke ruled that MIT graduates Anton and James Peraire-Bueno were cleared of all three charges—wire fraud, conspiracy to commit fraud, and conspiracy to commit money laundering—and dismissed the case without a retrial.

It happened in April 2023, under the codename Omakase. The brothers first placed eight bait transactions to lure Ethereum sandwich bots in, then exploited a vulnerability in the MEV-Boost relay software to obtain the contents of the entire block in advance. They reassembled the block themselves and dumped all the coins the bots had just bought. The bots lost $25 million; the brothers’ validator nodes were penalized by just 1 ETH.

The judge’s exact words were stark: “Ethereum is a trustless, highly adversarial environment with no user agreement.” Wire fraud requires proof of a material misrepresentation, but the bait transactions made no promises at all. The relay software didn’t even check the altered fields, and the fake signature had no effect. She also cited case law: improper, offensive, or even despicable conduct does not amount to a crime.

The two were arrested in May 2024, and each charge carried a maximum sentence of 20 years. The jury deadlocked in November 2025, resulting in a mistrial. It took 1,324 days for the case to finally reach a conclusion. Of the $25 million, only $3 million was frozen; the rest had been transferred out by October 2023.

The case could have significant ripple effects: Wall Street is pushing tokenized stocks, and in September the SEC asked trading venues to disclose their MEV policies—even if they don’t have one. Legally, front-running on-chain is still a gray area.

The website you check for crypto prices every day has been bought by Solana.

On November 17, the closing day of Breakpoint in London, the Solana Foundation announced that it had acquired a majority stake in CoinGecko. Vibhu Norby, the Foundation’s head of product, confirmed it himself on X.

CoinGecko is a veteran price-tracking website founded in 2014 by Malaysians Bobby Ong and TM Lee. It’s been around for 12 years, with 18 million registered users, 50 million visits and 200 million page views a month, and 180,000 institutions and apps rely on its API.

Here’s the interesting part: neither side has disclosed a word about the price, how much equity was acquired, or how the deal was done. CoinGecko’s own announcement was even more cautious, saying only that it had “received support from the Solana Foundation”—without mentioning equity at all.

The next steps are clear: CoinGecko’s website, GeckoTerminal, and app will integrate native Solana trading, so users can place orders right after checking prices. Its data and API will also expand to cover on-chain assets, derivatives, and RWAs. The founders have said the operating structure will remain unchanged, coverage will continue across all chains, data methodologies will stay public, and the commitment to neutrality will remain intact.

There’s precedent for this: Binance acquired CoinMarketCap in 2020. Then, in January this year, CoinDesk reported that CoinGecko had hired investment bank Moelis to explore a sale, with a possible valuation close to $500 million—but that was a rumored price from the start of the year, not the price of this deal. Don’t mix them up.

Betting on what Trump will say was generating $90 million in monthly trading volume. Now regulators have stepped in and shut it down.

On November 13, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) ordered prediction market Kalshi to halt its Trump “mention markets.” These markets let people bet on which words or nicknames Trump would use in public speeches. They were part of the TRUMPSAY series, and a winning contract paid $1.

This was no small business: monthly trading volume reached $90 million. But the format was too easy to exploit. White House teleprompter operator Gabriel Perez could see speech scripts an hour in advance. He used that information to bet on 14 markets, winning 39 out of 43 contracts and earning $107,000. He was then banned for three years, fined $65,000, and ordered to forfeit all his winnings.

The CFTC had warned on September 22 that contracts betting on what a person will say are inherently vulnerable to manipulation. Kalshi went ahead and launched them on October 1 without updating its certification. The CFTC has now issued a final warning: by December 11, Kalshi must respond in writing and show that its original certification was not false. This is not yet a final ruling, though.

Kalshi’s CEO said the company disagrees with the decision, but it has complied for now. Markets on what Vice President Vance, New York City Mayor Mamdani, and others will say are still available. Some sports markets have already been paused.

According to PANews on November 18, citing monitoring by Blockaid, K3 Capital’s sBOLD vault on Ethereum was attacked, with approximately $3.43 million stolen across around 34 transactions. The attack is still ongoing. My assessment is that this was not simply an external theft, but more likely a “self-liquidation arbitrage” targeting the vault’s internal accounting and liquidation pathways. This assessment depends on subsequent on-chain data confirming that the attacker did in fact complete the asset swaps via the pathway described above. If the vault’s remaining assets and the flow of funds to the attacker’s addresses indicate that the funds came from another source, this analysis of the mechanism will need to be revised.

Based on the information disclosed so far, the attack can be broken down into four steps: using a flash loan to obtain wstETH, “self-liquidating” the attacker’s own debt position in Liquity V2 and depositing into the stability pool, minting sBOLD shares at a low price, then swapping the collateral and redeeming other depositors’ BOLD. This suggests that the key issue is not the flash loan itself—it merely provides the initial capital—but whether the liquidation and stability pool mechanisms allow the same party to conveniently obtain both minted shares and swapped collateral when its debt position is liquidated. If this pathway is confirmed, the damage would extend beyond the balance-sheet assets of a single vault: it would undermine the backing for other depositors’ BOLD redemptions.

It is important to distinguish facts from inferences. The approximately $3.43 million in losses, around 34 transactions, and the ongoing attack are facts disclosed by Blockaid. Whether a flaw in the stability pool’s design was the root cause is currently only a line of inquiry in my assessment; this summary does not provide information on whether any Liquity V2 parameters were changed. Three conditions are worth tracking next: the scale of the vault’s remaining assets, the flow of funds to the attacker’s addresses, and whether any stability pool parameters have changed. If all three are consistent with the “self-liquidation arbitrage” pathway, confidence in this assessment will increase. If the fund flows point to other contracts or an external private key compromise, the analysis will need to be revisited. This article does not constitute investment advice.

$ETH

据PANews 11月18日援引Blockaid监测，以太坊上K3 Capital的sBOLD金库遭攻击，约343万美元被窃取，涉及约34笔交易，且攻击仍在持续。我的判断是：这不是一次单纯的外部盗取，而更像一次针对金库内部会计与清算路径的“自清算套利”。这一判断成立的前提，是后续链上数据能证实攻击者确实按上述路径完成了资产置换；若金库剩余资产与攻击者地址资金流向显示资金来自其他环节，则本文的机制拆解需要修正。

按已披露信息，攻击链条可以拆成四步：闪电贷获取wstETH，在Liquity V2对自身债仓进行“自清算”并存入稳定池，低价铸造sBOLD份额，随后置换抵押品并赎回其他存款人的BOLD。据此推断，问题的关键不在闪电贷本身——它只是提供启动资金——而在于清算与稳定池机制是否让同一主体能在债仓被清算时同时获得份额铸造与抵押品置换的便利。若这一路径成立，受损的就不只是单一金库的账面资产，而是其他存款人BOLD的兑付基础。

需要区分事实与推断。约343万美元、约34笔交易、攻击仍在持续，是Blockaid披露的事实；稳定池设计缺陷是否为根因，目前只是我的观察方向，本次摘要未提供Liquity V2相关参数是否被调整。接下来值得跟踪三个验证条件：金库剩余资产规模、攻击者地址资金流向、稳定池参数是否出现变更。三者若与“自清算套利”路径吻合，判断增强；若资金流向指向其他合约或外部私钥泄露，则需重新拆解。本文不构成投资建议。

translatedData.title: Trading Discipline | Five Rules I Keep Beside My Screen—Sharing Them Exactly as They Are
translatedData.subTitle:
On emotional days, people forget all the rules, so I wrote them down and posted them where I can see them:

1. Write down your stop-loss level before entering a trade. If you can’t, don’t enter.
2. Never risk more than 2% of your capital on a single trade. No exceptions.
3. Never add to a losing position or average down.
4. After three losses in a row, stop trading for the day. Just watch—don’t trade.
5. Withdraw part of your profits. Taking money out helps keep your mindset in check.

Just five rules, and not one of them is about “how to read the market.” Because the reason people lose big money is never
that they misread the market—it’s that their execution falls apart. Let’s keep each other accountable.

translatedData.title: Trading Psychology | Getting Rich Slowly: What Compounding Really Looks Like in Crypto
translatedData.subTitle:
Everyone wants to double their money overnight, but the people who truly hold on to their money in this market are the ones who “get rich slowly.”
Let’s do the math: earning just 1% a day adds up to 12 times your money over 250 trading days in a year; earning a steady 10% a month
adds up to 30 times your money over three years. It doesn’t sound thrilling, but it has one magical quality—it doesn’t rely on luck.

Doubling your money depends on market conditions; compounding depends on discipline. Market opportunities have to be waited for; discipline is up to you. Don’t set your goal
as “doubling your money this week.” Set it as “zero major mistakes this week.” The money from the former is given by the market;
the ability from the latter is yours. The market opens every day, but only those who preserve their capital are qualified to keep playing.

I just mentioned this a couple of days ago, and now there’s new progress. CoinShares has liquidated its ETH and SOL holdings, cashing out a total of $40 million, and is directly using that money for share buybacks. In plain terms, this is telling the market: our finances are stable, and we’re optimistic about the company’s future. But the issue is that selling these crypto assets is, in effect, weakening the company’s footprint in the digital currency space. Is this a strategic pullback or short-term cashing out? Especially with ETH down to $1,795.38 and SOL only at $74.36, turning around to buy back now isn’t cheap.

Impact on the market
- Short term: this $40 million buyback may temporarily lift CoinShares’ stock price, but the positive effect is likely to fade because the crypto assets are gone and the company ecosystem is actually harmed.
- Medium term: looking at the industry landscape, CoinShares’ move may prompt other institutions to follow suit, selling crypto assets and shifting toward traditional investments. In the long run, that would be negative for crypto market sentiment.

My view
CoinShares’ move feels more like an unwilling choice between BTC at $64,076.79 and ETH at $1,795.38. In the short term, the buyback can stabilize the stock price, but in the long run, selling core assets is like cutting off one’s own arm. 新比特币巨鲸最近账上亏了5.79亿美元，说明市场恐慌情绪在蔓延。

最近有报道说，不少新晋的比特币大玩家——也就是那些持有数千万美元以上比特币的人——突然亏了一大笔钱。具体来说，他们一共损失了5.79亿美元。这些新鲸鱼通常对市场比较敏感，他们的亏损往往反映了市场情绪的变化。现在他们亏钱，说明最近市场波动确实很大，可能是很多人在恐慌性抛售，导致比特币价格跟着往下掉。这5.79亿美元只是他们账面上的损失，具体是卖币还是因为其他原因还不清楚，但肯定是踩了市场的大坑。

The number I stared at the longest wasn’t the candlestick chart—it was my own buy-in price.

Only later did I realize: the market has no idea what price you bought in at.

Your cost basis exists only in your own account. The coin’s price won’t go up just because it’s getting closer to your entry price. The order book only shows buy and sell orders—there’s no column for “people who haven’t broken even yet.”

Here’s the mistake I made: I treated “breaking even” as a price level to wait for. More often than not, all I got was another stretch of sideways trading, while the opportunities in other coins came and went.

Your cost basis is your own account—not the market’s.

translatedData.content:
ETH｜Breaking down ETHW’s quarterly report: flows versus gains｜Asset growth isn’t the same as new buying

I remain cautious and want to see whether outflows can stop first. Looking through the quarterly report that Bitwise Ethereum ETF (ETHW) filed with the U.S. SEC for the quarter ended September 30, there is an easily overlooked distinction: the fund’s net assets rose from about $168.466 million at the end of June to about $296.910 million at the end of September, nearly doubling. But the report also disclosed that during the quarter, share creations added about 22,524.76 ETH, redemptions removed about 17,948.12 ETH, and approximately 51.95 ETH was used to pay management fees. Based on these three items, the net increase in ETH holdings was about 4,524.70 ETH—far less than the asset growth might intuitively suggest. The report explains that the change in valuation was mainly due to ETH’s reference price rising from $1,576.51 to $2,673.48 during the quarter. This is historical information as of the end of September; it should not be presented as institutional buying on November 18.

This breakdown is more useful for assessing today’s trading: a fund’s net assets equal the number of coins it holds multiplied by their price, less fees and other items. When prices rise, assets under management can grow mainly because of price revaluation, without corresponding to an equivalent amount of net spot buying. Conversely, active ETF trading on the secondary market does not necessarily mean new shares were created that day. To assess marginal demand, we also need to track primary-market creations and redemptions, the fund’s actual coin holdings, and daily net flows. The ETHW quarterly report also notes that share creations and redemptions can be settled in kind with ETH or in cash. These mechanisms differ, as does their short-term impact on spot trading, so not all trading volume should be treated as “buying” in the same way.

The signals the market is giving right now are weak. When I checked ETH/USDT on Binance, the price was about $1,794.63, down roughly 1.62% over 24 hours, with a low of $1,751.39 and a high of $1,836. Farside’s available summary table shows net outflows of about $29.1 million from U.S. spot ETH funds on November 17. That single-day figure and ETHW’s holdings at the end of September are not measured over the same period, and they do not prove that all funds are selling. ETH is still among the trending topics on Square over the past six hours, but trending topics are not net inflows. In the short term, I see around $1,750 as support and around $1,835 as the upper level that needs to be reclaimed. If the price breaks below $1,750 and then fails to recover it on a rebound, my rebound thesis is invalidated.

If I were trading this myself, I would sit out for now and not buy the dip just because the quarterly report showed growth in net assets. content:
ETH｜ETHW季报拆开资金与涨幅｜不把资产增长当成新买盘

我的态度仍是谨慎，先看资金能否止住流出。翻看Bitwise Ethereum ETF（ETHW）提交美国SEC的截至9月30日季度报告，有个容易被忽略的差别：基金净资产从6月底约1.68466亿美元升到9月底约2.96910亿美元，看起来接近翻倍；但报告同时披露，该季度因份额创设增加约22,524.76枚ETH，因赎回减少约17,948.12枚，另有约51.95枚用于支付管理费。按这三项计算，ETH数量净增加约4,524.70枚，远小于净资产涨幅给人的直觉。报告解释，估值变化主要来自季度内ETH参考价格从1,576.51美元升至2,673.48美元。这里是截至9月底的历史情况，不能写成11月18日机构增持。

这个拆分对今天的交易判断更有用：基金净资产等于币的数量乘价格，再扣除费用等项目；上涨时资产规模变大，可以主要是价格重估，未必对应等额现货净买入。反过来，二级市场ETF成交活跃，也不必然等于当日新增创设。真正要判断边际需求，还要追踪一级市场申赎、基金实际币数以及当日净流量。ETHW季报还说明，份额创设和赎回可以通过实物ETH或现金完成，机制不同，短时对现货交易的影响也不同，不能把所有交易量都套进同一条“买盘”公式。

市场眼前给出的信号偏弱。查询币安ETH/USDT时，现价约1,794.63美元，24小时跌约1.62%，区间低点1,751.39、高点1,836；Farside现有汇总表显示11月17日美国现货ETH基金合计净流出约2,910万美元。这个单日数字与9月底ETHW的季度持仓不是同一时间口径，也不能据此判断所有基金都在卖。广场近六小时热搜仍有ETH，但热搜不是净流入。短线我把1,750附近视为防守线，1,835附近视为需重新夺回的上沿；如果跌破1,750后反抽站不回，反弹判断被推翻。

如果是我自己交易，此刻不参与，不因为季报净资产增长就抄底。我只做不超过总资金4%的ETH现货试探：先等一小时收在1,820美元上方，再回踩1,805至1,820区间守住才分两笔买入；第一目标1,835，先减半，第二目标1,875，余仓到位平仓。硬止损在1,775，若成交后连续一小时收回1,805下方也平仓。若价格先跌破1,750，则取消这套多头计划，等待新的基金资金数据与价格重新企稳。仓位和止损先定，再谈方向，不用杠杆放大一个尚未确认的信号。

资料：Bitwise Ethereum ETF向SEC提交的2026年三季报；Farside ETH ETF资金表；币安ETH/USDT行情，11月18日晚间查询。#ETH
以上仅为个人市场观察，不构成投资建议。
